highlighted.tagline: Formula bar and inline formula editor
highlighted.whyItMatters: The new `FormulaBuilder` plugin adds a formula bar and an inline formula editor with colored references. Users can pick cell, range, and header references, get autocomplete and function help, and see formula error indicators.
The new `SheetsBar` plugin renders a tab bar above or below the grid, so users can switch between the sheets of a multi-sheet workbook. Each sheet has its own data, settings, and view state.

The new `ImportFile` plugin loads an `.xlsx` workbook into the grid. It reads cell types and formats, formulas, merged cells, frozen panes, hidden rows and columns, and comments. A built-in XLSX engine reads and writes `.xlsx` files, so `importFile` and `exportFile` no longer need ExcelJS. A setup that passes `engines: { xlsx: ExcelJS }` keeps working.

The `rowSelection` option adds a checkbox to every row and a select all checkbox in the header. The selection follows its rows when users sort, filter, move, add, or remove rows, and it works with server-side data and nested rows.

highlighted.tagline: The evaluation license key is gone
highlighted.whyItMatters: Handsontable 19.0 no longer accepts the evaluation license key, or the constant that holds it in the Angular wrapper. A grid that still uses it shows a lock screen, so get a trial, sponsored, or commercial key before you upgrade. Handsontable 18.1 and older still accept the old key.
